title: TrueNorth level
description: One playable level, `content/levels/<id>.json`. This file is the whole level: parallax layers, ground polyline, camera, spawn, points of interest, character placements, locomotion tuning and the asset manifest. Adding a level is this file plus assets — if a level needs an engine change, this schema is wrong (docs/plan/slices.md, Rules).

subject.description: The teaching remit of this level's quest, and the question bank the scheduler draws from for it. Not a claim about what the level's landmark blurbs or dialogue teach (ADR-0030).

order.description: Position in the world map, 1-10. Unlocking is game.config's job, not this file's.

title.description: The level's name, carried in the document rather than in a locale bundle (ADR-0010).

size.description: World size in design-resolution pixels. The camera clamps to it and the ground polyline must fit inside it.

spawn.description: Where the player starts, in design-resolution pixels.

weather.description: What falls across the play area on this level, decided per level from its season as its art sheet states it (assets/style/<id>-level.md). `snow` draws falling snow, as many flakes as the visual tier allows and none under reduced motion; `none` draws no falling weather at any tier, so the scene probe's `data-particles` reads 0. Required, with no default: a default of `snow` put winter on eight summer and autumn levels, and a default of `none` would take it off the two winter ones the moment a level forgot to say. tests/unit/contracts/a-level-snows-only-where-its-art-sheet-says.test.ts holds every level to its sheet.

playerCostume.description: What the player wears on this level: a `costume` option of the character rig (content/characters/rig.json), decided per level from the season its art sheet states (assets/style/<id>-level.md names it beside its weather). `parka` is the winter kit; `jacket` is the warm-weather clothes. It dresses the player only: the officer and the guide wear what their artboards pin. Required, with no default: the rig's parka dressed the player for January on eight summer and autumn levels because no level could say otherwise, and a `jacket` default would take the coat off the two winter ones the first time a level forgot. tests/unit/contracts/a-level-dresses-the-player-for-its-season.test.ts holds every level to its sheet and every option to the rig.

theme.description: Palette override for this level. Absent means the renderer keeps game.config's theme.

territory.description: Whose land this level is set on, stated as a citable fact. Required on every level: every place in Canada is on someone's territory, and a level that omits this has not decided, it has just not said (docs/content-review.md 10).

ground.description: The walkable/skateable surface as a polyline in design-resolution pixels, ordered left to right. Slope between consecutive points is what LocomotionIntent.slope samples.

layers.description: Parallax layers, any order; the renderer sorts by depth and keeps as many as the graphics preset allows.

groundDressing.description: The art drawn over the ground fill, below the walking line (ADR-0042). Every layer draws under the ground polygon, so without this the lower third of every screen was one flat colour. Required, with no default: every level's ground line sits near world y 1280 (art bible section 6), so every level has that band to dress.

locomotion.description: Locomotion modes this level offers, in the order the player unlocks them. The first is the mode the player spawns in. Walking and skating differ by these numbers alone (slice 1 task 1.14).

rides.description: What carries the player in a mode the rig cannot carry them in by itself: a vehicle or an animal drawn around the player, at the player, every frame they move by that mode (ADR-0031). Optional, because a level whose player walks, skates, sleds or cycles draws that on the rig (assets/style/rig-contract.md section 11) and declares none. At most one ride per mode, and a ride's `mode` must be one of this level's `locomotion[].mode`: JSON Schema cannot compare an array item with a sibling array, so the parser refuses both at load and tests/unit/contracts/level-art-is-placed-where-it-is-drawn.test.ts refuses them in CI.

assets.description: The art this level needs, by KEY. Optional since ADR-0020: the loader is manifest-driven, so a level does not have to restate what it already names in layers[].key, pois[].artKey and characters[]. What a human writes here is key and kind; url, bytes and decodedBytes are build-derived and belong to assets/dist/manifest.json, which is the only place they can be true after a content-hashing build. The per-level texture budget is enforced from the manifest, not from this array - see ADR-0020 for why the previous arrangement left TN-LEVEL-02's runtime refusal summing an empty list.

textureBudgetBytes.description: Author-declared decoded-texture ceiling for this level, at most 64 MB (CLAUDE.md, Budgets).

territoryStatement.title: Territory statement
territoryStatement.description: The first line of the level's "About this place" panel (docs/content-review.md 10.2): a territorial FACT, sourced and verifiable, not an acknowledgement. The distinction is the whole of 10.1 and it is load-bearing. "Ottawa is on the unceded traditional territory of the Algonquin Anishinaabe Nation" is a citable statement an agent may write and a verifier may check. "We acknowledge that we live and work on..." is a statement of relationship in the project's own voice, and no agent may write it: a model has no relationship to acknowledge, and a generated acknowledgement is words asserting something that was never true. There is deliberately no field for one here. If the project owner writes one, it is signed and it lives in README.md, where the project speaks for itself. ONE CITATION, AND THE NAMES COME OUT OF IT (ADR-0051): the statement cites exactly one source, in `fact.source`, and every name in `nations` must be a name that source prints for a people. There is no second citation to write, which is what makes a statement whose names come from one page and whose sentence comes from another unrepresentable rather than merely discouraged - it was the shipped state on seven of the ten levels.

nations.description: The nations whose territory this is, each named as the cited source names them, and each named as that nation names itself. The same deny-list as a character's nation: a category word is a build failure, because a list the panel heads "Named in this statement" carrying the single word "Inuit" is the generic-person failure 3.1 exists to prevent. MAY BE EMPTY (ADR-0051), and only when the cited source names no people for this place - in which case `nationsAbsentBecause` is required and records that judgement. The deny-list is anchored to the whole value, so a longer name a source really prints ("Metis of the Red River") is legal and a bare category word is not; which of those a phrase is, is the author's proposal and the verifier's judgement, not a regex's.

nationsAbsentBecause.description: Why this statement names no people. Required if and only if `nations` is empty, and forbidden otherwise (see the conditional below). An empty list on its own would spell three different states one way: an author who had not got round to it, an author who could not find a name, and an author recording that the cited source names nobody. This is the third, recorded rather than defaulted - the shape factClaim.factual and characterDocument.indigenous already use. One value today: a second reason is a schema change and an ADR, because any other reason for printing no name is a decision somebody should have to argue.

statement.description: The fact, in plain language, in both languages. Shown in the panel, never as a modal on level entry and never as anything a player taps past to reach gameplay - which is what teaches that it is a thing you tap past. It may use the cited source's own term where that source uses it, marked as the source's (docs/content-review.md 9.2) - that is prose a reader can weigh, and it is a different object from `nations`, which is a list of names.

fact.description: Source and verification for the statement, checked under ADR-0003 like any other claim, and the ONE citation this statement carries: the names in `nations` come from this source too (ADR-0051). `factual` must be true - a territory statement that claimed nothing would not be one, and a false one would draw an unsourced sentence about whose land this is past every gate, because adjudicateClaim correctly treats a non-factual block as drawable. That rule is held by parseLevelDocument and by tests/unit/contracts/a-territory-names-what-its-source-prints.test.ts rather than here, for the reason ADR-0051 section 4 records.

sourcePublisher.description: Who published the source cited in `fact.source`. The "About this place" panel draws this as the text of its source link and `fact.source.url` as the link's target, so the panel names where the STATEMENT comes from - which is what 10.2 asks for and what the panel did not do before ADR-0051: it drew `nationSource`, where the NAMES came from, which on seven of the ten levels was a different page from the one the sentence was quoted from, and on five of those a different body. It is a copy of the `publisher` of the register named by `fact.source.sourceId`, and a checked copy: the runtime cannot read a source register (there is no port for one), so the string is carried here and pinned to the register by tests/unit/contracts/a-territory-names-what-its-source-prints.test.ts.

allOf.$comment: ADR-0051: an empty `nations` carries the judgement that made it empty, and a non-empty one cannot carry that judgement as well. Only property names this object already declares appear here (ADR-0007), and the `else` follows character.schema.json's shape for the same rule about `nation`.

cameraTuning.title: Camera tuning
cameraTuning.description: How the camera follows the player. Portrait only (ADR-0002), so the vertical numbers matter as much as the horizontal ones.

followLerp.description: 0-1 per frame at 60 fps. 1 is rigid; reduced motion clamps this down, it does not read it from here.

deadZone.description: Half-size of the box the player may move inside before the camera follows, in design-resolution pixels.

offset.description: Where the player sits in frame. A negative y lifts the player above centre so the lower third stays free for the question card (ADR-0002).

zoom.description: Fixed zoom for the level. Design resolution is 1080x1920, so 1 shows the level at authored scale.

parallaxLayer.title: Parallax layer
parallaxLayer.description: One scrolling band of the backdrop. Sky and ground panels on desktop extend the outermost layers (ADR-0002).

key.description: Texture key, matching a LevelAssetRef key or a frame inside one of its atlases.

depth.description: Render order, low to high. The graphics preset's parallaxLayers count keeps the highest-depth layers and drops the rest, so decoration must sit at a lower depth than anything load-bearing.

scrollFactor.description: Camera-relative scroll rate per axis. 0 is pinned to the viewport, 1 moves with the world.

offset.description: Placement in design-resolution pixels before scrolling is applied.

repeatX.description: Tile horizontally to fill the level width. False draws the texture once at offset.

groundDressing.title: Ground dressing
groundDressing.description: A horizontally repeating strip drawn over the ground fill and under every landmark, character and ride (ADR-0042): the near part of the ground the player walks on, seen closer. It is fixed to the world, so it goes by under the player as the ground does, and it is not a parallax layer: layers draw under the ground polygon and the visual tier drops them, and this is drawn over the polygon at every tier. The HUD covers the bottom of the canvas (at 390 x 844, the canvas below about world 1440 with a prompt showing and below about 1810 without), so a strip keeps its detail in its first rows.

key.description: Texture key, `<levelId>-<file>` for a source under assets/src/svg/<levelId>/, pinned to 1x by its filename so an art pixel is a design pixel. The texture's width is the tile; the strip is drawn one screen wide.

topY.description: The world row of the strip's first row. At or below the LOWEST point of the ground polyline (its largest y), so that no row of the strip is ever drawn above the ground, over the backdrop, on a level whose ground falls away. JSON Schema cannot compare a number with an array, so the parser refuses a strip that starts higher, and tests/unit/contracts/level-art-is-placed-where-it-is-drawn.test.ts refuses it in CI.

pointOfInterest.title: Point of interest
pointOfInterest.description: A landmark the player taps to engage. The blurb is the fact it teaches, so a POI is content, not decoration; decoration is a parallax layer.

blurb.description: Plain-language description shown when the player engages, roughly CLB 4 (CLAUDE.md, Accessibility).

fact.description: Whether the blurb states a fact about Canada and, if so, its source and verification. A landmark blurb that says "the Peace Tower was completed in 1927" is a claim, and ADR-0003 governs it exactly as it governs a question.

artKey.description: Texture key for the landmark art.

radiusPx.description: Engagement radius in design-resolution pixels. At least 44 pt of screen at design scale (CLAUDE.md, Accessibility).

questId.description: Quest this POI GIVES or advances, when it is a quest target. It could always advance one; since ADR-0029 it can also be the `giver`, which is how `peggys-cove` and `the-north` hold a quest without drawing a figure - a plaque offers, reminds and closes, and the level's placement of it is what says the giver has no rig and no face. When this POI IS the giver, the quest's `giver` equals this POI's `id` and this field equals that quest's `id`; the gate checks both halves and refuses a giver matched by zero placements or by two.

levelCharacter.title: Level character
levelCharacter.description: Where a character document is placed in this level. The character's own art, rig and skins live in `content/characters/<id>.json`; only placement belongs here.

questId.description: Quest this character gives or advances, when they are a quest target. A character is ONE KIND of giver, not the definition of one (ADR-0029): the sibling field on `pointOfInterest` is the other, and the quest document names an id without saying which list it is in, because this document is the one that knows.

ride.title: Ride
ride.description: A vehicle or animal the player rides, placed by the engine at the player's position every frame rather than at a fixed point in the world. It is level art registered to the rider, not a character: the rig poses the rider with `<mode>/<state>` states (assets/style/rig-contract.md section 11) and this record says where in the ride's own art the rider sits and where that art meets the level's ground. Every file in `art` shares one size and one registration, so one `riderAnchor` and one `groundLineY` serve them all. Drawn only while the player moves by `mode`. The layers are level art and are charged to this level's texture budget alone, which is the reason a ride is not rig equipment: equipment lives on the shared atlas and is charged to every level.

mode.description: The locomotion mode this ride carries the player in. One of this level's `locomotion[].mode`, and no other ride on the level names it.

art.description: The ride's layers, each drawn either behind the rider or in front of them. A car the rider sits inside is a `front` layer with the rider showing through its glass; a horse would be a `behind` body and a `front` near-side leg. At most one layer per side.

riderAnchor.description: Where the rider's sole line meets their centre line, in the art's own pixels measured from its top-left corner (its SVG viewBox). The rig's `characterSpace.soleY` and `centreX` land on this point, so a seated pose authored with its feet on the sole line has them on this floor. The art ships at 1x, so an art pixel is a design pixel.

groundLineY.description: The row of the art, in its own pixels from the top, that lies on the level's ground polyline under the rider. The art's bottom row for a ride standing on the walking line. A row above the bottom for a ride drawn on a nearer line across the ground fill, which is what lets the landmarks and people placed on the walking line stand beyond it instead of being hidden by it.

turnsWithRider.description: true when the art mirrors about the rider as the rider turns, as an animal walking head first does. false when it does not: a train backs up without turning round, and its passenger turns in their seat.

backingMaxSpeed.description: How fast a ride that does not turn with its rider may back up, in design px/s (ADR-0043). Backing is never automatic: the ride moves backwards only while the player presses back, brakes to rest on the mode's own brake when they let go, and waits there until they press forward or engage something. This caps it, so going back to something passed is a slow move and not a run at cruise speed. Only for a ride whose `turnsWithRider` is false: a ride that turns faces the way it goes and never backs up. Absent, the mode's own `maxSpeed` caps it.

rideArt.title: Ride art
rideArt.description: One layer of a ride: a texture key, and which side of the rider it is drawn on.

key.description: Texture key, `<levelId>-<file>` for a source under assets/src/svg/<levelId>/, pinned to 1x by its filename. The layer's still: the whole layer when it declares no `cycle`, and the one frame drawn under reduced motion, at every speed, when it does (ADR-0035).

side.description: `behind` draws under every part of the rider; `front` draws over every part of the rider and still under the tappable marks, which must never be hidden by the thing they sit above.

rideCycle.title: Ride cycle
rideCycle.description: Frames for one layer of a ride, so an animal's legs move while the ground goes by (ADR-0035). Advanced by distance travelled and not by time: one frame per `framePx` of travel, so the gait keeps pace with the ground at every speed and stops when the player stops. At rest the layer draws `rest`. Under reduced motion it draws the layer's `key` and never advances, and that is the engine's rule rather than a level's (CLAUDE.md, Accessibility), which is why no field here could express otherwise. Every frame shares the layer's size and registration, so the one `riderAnchor` seats the rider in every frame. Optional, because a ride whose art does not change as it travels (a car on a track) needs none.

rest.description: Texture key of the frame drawn while the ride is not moving, under the same rules as `rideArt.key`. May be the layer's `key`.

frames.description: Texture keys of the gait, in the order travel plays them, under the same rules as `rideArt.key`. The cycle repeats after the last. May include the layer's `key`, which costs no second texture.

framePx.description: Design pixels travelled per frame. The whole cycle is `framePx` times the number of frames: one stride for an animal.

rideFootprint.title: Ride footprint
rideFootprint.description: The span of the ride's art, in its own pixels, inside which a figure standing beyond the ride reads as being in it: seen through its glass, or sitting where the rider sits. A car names its glazing, not its steel flank, because a person behind a solid side reads as standing beyond the train; an animal names its saddle, the seat the rider is seen in, because a person behind its solid body reads as standing beyond it. The engine brings a drive to rest so that no character in reach stands inside this span (ADR-0037). Measured from the art's left edge and pinned to 1x like `riderAnchor`, so an art pixel is a design pixel.

x.description: The span's left edge, in the art's own pixels from its left edge.

width.description: The span's width, in the art's own pixels.

rideBob.title: Ride bob
rideBob.description: A vertical rock the ride and its rider share, so a car rides its rail joints and an animal its gait. It grows with speed and is still at rest. Reduced motion holds it at zero, and that is the engine's rule rather than a level's (CLAUDE.md, Accessibility). Absent is still.

amplitudePx.description: Peak lift at cruise speed, design-resolution pixels.

periodPx.description: Distance travelled per rock, design-resolution pixels. A distance and not a time, so the rhythm follows the ground going by.

rideTrack.title: Ride track
rideTrack.description: What the ride runs on when that is not the level's own ground: a horizontally repeating strip drawn across the view and fixed to the world, so it scrolls past under the ride the way the ground does. It exists because a ride drawn on a nearer line than the walking line has nothing under it but ground fill, and a strip baked into the ride's own art would move with the ride and end where the art ends. Drawn above the ground and below every actor, and not subject to the parallax tier, because a train with no rails under it is floating.

artKey.description: Texture key of the repeating strip, under the same rules as `rideArt.key`.

topY.description: Where the strip's top edge sits, as a row in the ride's own art pixels. The strip does not share the ride's bob: it is the ground.

key.description: The key scenes and layers refer to this asset by.

url.description: BUILD-DERIVED. Path relative to the site base, as shipped under assets/dist. Optional since ADR-0020 and NOT hand-authorable: the pipeline content-hashes every output and emits a 1x and a 2x variant per key, so a path written by a person is wrong at the next `make assets` and names only one of the two scales. A level document names a KEY; assets/dist/manifest.json resolves it.

bytes.description: Transfer size at the WORST device scale, summed against the 8 MB per-level payload budget. Hand-written and machine-checked: scripts/lib/texture-memory.mjs asserts every declared figure against assets/dist/manifest.json, so this is a number somebody writes and CI re-derives - which is the arrangement ADR-0013 asks for, not the one it warns about.

decodedBytes.description: Decoded (not transfer) size for textures at the WORST device scale; 0 for non-texture assets. This is what TN-LEVEL-02 sums to refuse an over-budget level before any asset is fetched, so it stays REQUIRED - an optional one would default to zero and re-create the exact defect ADR-0020 records, a refusal that cannot fire. ADR-0013 forbids trusting a decodedBytes nobody re-derives; scripts/lib/texture-memory.mjs re-derives it from the manifest, which is what makes a hand-written figure legitimate here.

locomotionMode.title: Locomotion mode
locomotionMode.description: Every way TrueNorth crosses Canada. A mode is a NAME over a tuning record and carries no behaviour of its own: there is exactly one `step` in app/adapters/phaser/locomotion.ts, every mode goes through it, and a gate strips the comments out of that file and fails if a single mode name survives in the code. So the legal set is data, and it lives in content/game.config.json#/locomotionModes rather than in this enum (ADR-0023). It was a closed enum of eight, written in slice 0 against ten planned levels before any of them existed, and it was wrong at the first level that was not Ottawa - a toboggan for Quebec City. A mode name is validated against the config, not against this schema; the same treatment `LevelId` already gets, and for the same reason.

movementDrive.title: Movement drive
movementDrive.description: held: the player holds to move and stops on release (walk, bike, skate). auto: movement is continuous and the player only steers or brakes (train; also every mode when the auto-move accessibility option is on).

jumpAffordance.title: Jump affordance
jumpAffordance.description: What a tap does when the player is not touching an NPC or POI. One-thumb traversal, never a trick system (CLAUDE.md, Traversal).

maxHoldMs.description: Hold-to-jump-higher window; 0 makes the jump fixed-height.

airControl.description: Fraction of ground acceleration available in the air.

maxJumps.description: 1 for a single jump; 2 for a bunny-hop mode.

interactionAffordance.title: Interaction affordance
interactionAffordance.description: How close, and how still, the player must be to engage an NPC or POI in this mode.

requiresStop.description: Some modes (canoe, train) require coming to rest before engaging.

whileMoving.description: Whether a tap engages while moving, or only when idle.

approachSpeed.description: Speed the mode decelerates to when an interaction starts, in px/s.

locomotionAnimationBinding.title: Locomotion animation binding
locomotionAnimationBinding.description: Character state-machine inputs this mode drives. Every name must be an input content/characters/rig.json declares, of the type its field names: tests/unit/contracts/a-level-binds-only-what-the-rig-declares.test.ts holds every level to that. `airborneInput` and `brakeTrigger` were removed on 2026-09-14: every level bound them to `airborne` and `brake`, the rig declares `grounded` (not its negation) and no brake, nothing read either field, and every level logged the two names at open (assets/style/rig-contract.md section 11.6).

jumpTrigger.description: Trigger input fired at take-off. Absent when the mode cannot jump.

landTrigger.description: Trigger input fired on ground contact. Absent when the mode cannot jump.

locomotionTuning.title: Locomotion tuning
locomotionTuning.description: Everything a level must provide to offer a mode. Every difference between walking and dogsledding is a number or a null in this record.

deceleration.description: px/s^2 while input is released - friction, edging, paddling drag.

turnAcceleration.description: px/s^2 while input is held against the current direction - the brake, and then the turn. Must sit strictly between deceleration and acceleration: above deceleration so holding the other way stops you in a shorter distance than a free glide, and below acceleration so reaching cruise speed the other way takes longer than starting from rest (TN-LEVEL-03). The band is asserted by tests/unit/contracts/locomotion-tuning-is-coherent.test.ts; JSON Schema cannot compare two sibling values.

glide.description: How much momentum survives an input release; ice and water sit near 1.

maxSpeedMultiplierDownhill.description: Speed cap on a downhill or tailwind segment, as a multiple of maxSpeed.

jump.description: null means this mode cannot jump (canoe, train).

interaction.description: null means this mode cannot engage; the player must dismount first.

labelKey.description: Localiser key naming the mode for the a11y live region and the HUD. A key, not inline text: a mode label is engine vocabulary reused by every level (ADR-0010).
